evaluation.subject: maths
evaluation.question: Use a graph to maximize Z = -x - y subject to x >= 0, y >= 0 and 2 <= x + y <= 6. Label the exact corners and the full set of optimal points.
must_show: labelled axes and solid parallel boundaries x + y = 2 and x + y = 6
only the closed first-quadrant quadrilateral between those lines shaded
the whole inner edge from (2, 0) to (0, 2) highlighted as optimal
must_not_show: the outer edge x + y = 6 identified as maximizing
only one inner-edge endpoint marked as the unique optimum
answer_facts: Corner objective values: Z(0, 2) = -2; Z(0, 6) = -6; Z(2, 0) = -2; Z(6, 0) = -6.
Maximum Z is -2 at every point (t, 2-t), 0 <= t <= 2.
The region is bounded; the maximum has infinitely many solutions.
